item.content:encoded:
Members of the Government gathered at Civic House this morning to pay their final respects to late Minister for Employment , Productivity and Workplace Relations Agni Deo Singh, remembering him as a leader who cared deeply for people and treated everyone with dignity and respect.

His casket was received by Minister for Policing Ioane Naivalurua, Acting Minister for Employment , Siromi Turaga, Permanent Secretary for Employment Maritino Nemani and other Ministry officials.

Turaga described Singh as a leader whose warmth and care left a lasting impression on those who worked alongside him.

item.title: 1,500 Fijian caregivers could work in Israel under proposed agreement
item.description: Fiji’s Ambassador to Israel, Jesoni Vitusagavulu says the first group of 25 caregivers is expected to arrive in Israel by December this year. He highlighted the proposed labour mobility arrangement while speaking at Ariel University as Fiji marked one year since establishing its diplomatic mission in Jerusalem.
item.content:encoded:
Fiji’s Ambassador to Israel, Jesoni Vitusagavulu says the first group of 25 caregivers is expected to arrive in Israel by December this year.

He highlighted the proposed labour mobility arrangement while speaking at Ariel University as Fiji marked one year since establishing its diplomatic mission in Jerusalem.

Vitusagavulu says the proposed agreement could see up to 1,500 Fijian caregivers work in Israel over the next 12 months.

He also highlighted opportunities for Fijians in agriculture, saying 20 additional students arrived in Israel last month for an 11-month agricultural internship programme, while another 50 students are expected in November.

Vitusagavulu says Fiji’s diplomatic presence in Israel is aimed at creating further opportunities in areas including agriculture, tourism, investment, exports and labour mobility.

He says progress has been made during the embassy’s first year and hopes cooperation between Fiji and Israel will continue to grow.

Fiji opened its Embassy in Jerusalem in September last year.

item.title: Former Corrections officer turns farming dream into award-winning business
item.description: Raj received the award at the National Agriculture Show in Labasa. He says farming was always something he wanted to pursue on a large scale, and the income he earned while working for the Corrections Service helped him invest in the business.
item.content:encoded:
Raj received the award at the National Agriculture Show in Labasa.

He says farming was always something he wanted to pursue on a large scale, and the income he earned while working for the Corrections Service helped him invest in the business.

Raj says when he and his wife Ranjini first bought their land, it was covered in bush and they did not know where to begin.

With support from his wife, family, workers and others who believed in his plans, they gradually transformed the land into a farming business.

Today, Raj has around 2,000 chickens producing about 55 trays of eggs a day, which are sold to market vendors.

The business has also expanded beyond poultry into goat and vegetable farming, while his wife looks after their honey production.

Six people are currently employed across Raj's poultry and goat farming operations.

Raj says their next goal is to expand further into watermelon and ginger farming.

He says he received a $31,000 grant through the Northern Development Programme and also secured a loan from the Fiji Development Bank to support the development of the business.

Raj says attending the National Agriculture Show has exposed him to modern farming setups and given him new ideas that he hopes to introduce on his own farm.

He is encouraging young people who are struggling to find work, to consider opportunities in agriculture rather than seeing white-collar employment as their only option.

Raj says farming can be challenging, but when approached as a business, it can generate income and create employment opportunities for others.

He has thanked his wife, workers, market vendors, financial institutions and others who supported him as he turned his farming dream into a growing business.

item.title: GCC welcomes Cabinet decision but calls for faster passage of legislation
item.description: In a statement, the Bose Levu Vakaturaga says it appreciates the Government’s decision to move forward with legislation to establish it under the Constitution and in law. However, it says the iTaukei have waited long enough for the restoration of their traditional governance institution, and is calling for the Bose Levu Vakaturaga Bill to be introduced in Parliament this month.
item.content:encoded:
In a statement, the Bose Levu Vakaturaga says it appreciates the Government’s decision to move forward with legislation to establish it under the Constitution and in law.

However, it says the iTaukei have waited long enough for the restoration of their traditional governance institution, and is calling for the Bose Levu Vakaturaga Bill to be introduced in Parliament this month.

Cabinet has endorsed the start of the stand-alone legislative process, with the Ministry of iTaukei Affairs required to carry out further consultations with relevant iTaukei institutions under section 11 of the iTaukei Affairs Act 1944 before the Bill returns to Cabinet for final consideration and introduction in Parliament.

The BLV says it is concerned that this process could result in further delays.

They have also raised concerns about Clause 1(2) of the draft Bill, which it says provides for the legislation to come into force on a date or dates appointed by the Minister through a Gazette notice.

The Council says this could mean that even after Parliament passes the legislation, parts of the law may not immediately come into effect.

They say this could delay the Bose Levu Vakaturaga receiving full corporate status, operational authority and its own financial arrangements.

The Council wants the clause amended so that the legislation comes into effect upon assent or on a fixed date.

They say the restoration of the institution should be immediate and complete once the legislation is passed.

The Bose Levu Vakaturaga has also stressed that it wants to operate independently of Government and without political interference.

They also say its authority should be based on its traditional governance role rather than being limited to an advisory or oversight role of the State.

The Bose Levu Vakaturaga says while it is ready to work constructively with the Government, it will continue pushing for what it describes as the full and meaningful restoration of the institution.

item.title: Ministry warns people with HIV not to stop treatment over herbal cure claims
item.description: People living with HIV are being urged not to stop taking their medication following false claims circulating on social media that HIV can be cured through herbal medicine. The Ministry of Health and Medical Services says a video circulating online claims that a person was cured of HIV through herbal medicine and that a health worker had confirmed the cure.
item.content:encoded:
People living with HIV are being urged not to stop taking their medication following false claims circulating on social media that HIV can be cured through herbal medicine.

The Ministry of Health and Medical Services says a video circulating online claims that a person was cured of HIV through herbal medicine and that a health worker had confirmed the cure.

The Ministry says there is no herbal, traditional, food or spiritual remedy anywhere in the world that has been proven to cure HIV.

It is reminding people living with HIV that antiretroviral therapy, or ART, works by stopping the virus from growing in the body and protecting the immune system.

ART is available free of charge at government health facilities for all Fijians.

The Ministry is also stressing that an undetectable viral load does not mean a person has been cured of HIV.

It says when a person's viral load is undetectable, they cannot pass HIV to their sexual partner, a principle known as Undetectable equals Untransmittable, or U=U.

However, the Ministry says the virus remains in the body and can return if treatment is stopped.

It says stopping ART can result in the person becoming unwell, damage to the immune system, transmission of HIV to others and drug resistance.

People using herbal or traditional remedies are being advised to continue taking their ART and inform their health worker so they can check whether the remedy is safe.

The Ministry says it has no record of any Ministry of Health facility or clinician confirming an HIV cure and has reminded health workers to provide advice in line with the National HIV Care and Antiretroviral Therapy Guidelines.

It is also urging the public not to share the video or shame, abuse or attempt to identify the person featured in it.

The Ministry says anyone who has stopped taking their HIV medication can return to care and will be supported without judgement.

Fiji Network Plus, the national network of people living with HIV, is supporting the Ministry's message and is urging people not to stop ART because of claims that herbs can cure HIV.

People with questions about HIV testing, treatment or the claim can contact the SRH and HIV Unit on 3316101.

item.title: From Italy to Fiji for the Yat Sen 90/40 Gala Night
item.description: Travelling all the way from Italy to the Vodafone Arena for the Yat Sen 90/40 Gala Night celebrations, Arthur Sorby returned to Fiji to reconnect with old friends during the three-day celebrations . Sorby and Lee were members of the Class of 1992, and the duo could not contain their excitement when they met at the Gala Night after so many years apart.
item.content:encoded:
Travelling all the way from Italy to the Vodafone Arena for the Yat Sen 90/40 Gala Night celebrations, Arthur Sorby returned to Fiji to reconnect with old friends during the three-day celebrations .

Sorby and Lee were members of the Class of 1992, and the duo could not contain their excitement when they met at the Gala Night after so many years apart.

Sorby says the trip had been well worth it, as he was able to reconnect with many of his old friends.

He says he attended all three days of the celebrations, describing the experience as both fun and hectic.

Sorby and Lee's message to current students was simple to live by the three Ds — dedication, determination and discipline, and they will achieve great things in life.
